newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures jerk to mostly firmer close.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures jerk to mostly firmer close.

text.p: U.S. debt futures jerked erratically in late afternoon trading, finally landing at mostly firmer levels by the close.
Futures swung between losses and gains several times during choppy turnover as the market eyed the Treasury's first auction of inflation-indexed 10-year T-notes.
After the auction, which traders said initially appeared to go well, brokers said one dealer bought some 2,000 March futures and lifted the listing to the day's high at 110-19/32.
Locals then sold, joined by paper sales, amid a dearth of bids, and futures quickly sagged back into the minus side.
"Everybody was anticipating a real good auction," said one floor broker. "Then the locals sold and pressed it. It was a frustrating day, a flighty day."

Another broker also noted market talk that one large entity, rumored to be an Asian central bank, purchased the bulk of the new indexed T-notes. They said that same entity had sold a huge amount of cash 10-year notes and some 2,000 March T-bond futures during the morning's abrupt pullback.
He figured that the central bank might have been rolling a long cash note position into the new indexed notes and hedging them with sales of T-bond futures.

Futures had lurched upward briefly and erased opening losses when December U.S. durable goods orders fell 1.7 percent and dropped 1.5 percent without defense orders. Economists had expected respective gains of 1.2 percent and 2.2 percent.
Technically, the ability of March T-bonds to recover and close above the 200-day moving average pegged at about 109-18/32 to 20/32 may deter some selling, chartists said.
But several said the market's weak price performance recently still boded for further downside soon.
"Technically, it still looks bad," said the second broker.

March T-bonds ended up 6/32 at 110-08/32, notes rose 5/32 to 108-02/32, muni-bonds gained 5/32 to 114-04/32, T-bills ended flat at 94.92, and June Eurodollars closed up one bp at 94.21. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
